# Exact canonical rustdoc paragraph: Nothing is left behind. Once polled, creation and cleanup run in tasks of their own, so the session is killed even if this future is dropped or the operation panics, while the Tokio runtime is alive. A cleanup failure then has no caller to reach; the `tracing` feature records it.
Blocking contract: Cancellation before creation starts leaves tmux untouched. After creation starts, the call waits for the resource ID and kills the session before reporting cancellation. Once the callback starts, cancellation is cooperative: its tmux operations observe the token. Cleanup runs before return and during panic unwinding, using an uncancelled handle.

# Exact canonical rustdoc paragraph: A runtime cannot be driven from within one, so [`crate::blocking::Runtime::run`] panics here. [`crate::blocking::Runtime::try_run`] returns this instead, for callers who would rather handle it: await the future directly.
Blocking contract: This variant describes nested runtime use in the native Tokio client. Blocking client methods do not construct or drive an async runtime.

# Exact canonical rustdoc paragraph: Nothing is left held by a drop. The lock is taken and released in tasks of their own, so a scope dropped while its lock is still queued unlocks once tmux grants it, as [`Self::lock_channel`] describes.
Blocking contract: Cancellation before locking leaves tmux untouched. Cancellation while queued returns to the caller; a worker keeps the queued request and releases any later grant. A callback already running must cooperate with the token. Cleanup runs before return and during panic unwinding.

# Exact canonical rustdoc paragraph: Nothing is left held. The lock is taken in a task of its own, so a lock that is dropped -- or that runs out of time -- while queued behind another locker is not withdrawn from tmux, which cannot withdraw one: it is granted in turn and released at once. Between those two, later lockers wait as they would for any other holder.
Blocking contract: Nothing is left held after cancellation. A lock cancelled or timed out while queued is not withdrawn from tmux, which cannot withdraw one: a worker retains it until it is granted, then releases it. Between grant and release, later lockers wait as they would for any other holder.
